title: How to build a pond that stays clear

lines.show: You want a {g:clear} pond in your garden.
So you dig a shallow hole
and lay a {y:liner} in it.
But a sharp stone pokes a {r:hole} in it.
So you lay {y:sand} and fleece underneath first.
Then summer comes, and the water turns {r:green}.
Too shallow, too warm.
So you dig a deep zone,
at least {y:80 centimeters}.
But you planted in garden {r:soil}.
It feeds the algae.
So you plant in plain {y:gravel} instead.
And you add lots of {y:plants}
to cover about a third of the surface.
Then rain washes {r:fertilizer} in from the lawn.
So you raise the {y:edge} above the ground.
In autumn, falling {r:leaves} rot on the bottom.
So you stretch a {y:net} over it.
{y:Congratulations}.
You built a pond
that stays {g:crystal clear}.
